messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

NOTE: Communications in your area are sometimes subject to routine monitoring by the authorities.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: The institutional foundations that held this regime together are visibly crumbling.
ATMOSPHERE: Strangers are approaching each other to talk about 'the situation' — the trust radius has expanded dramatically.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] a cabinet reshuffle was announced and then reversed within the same day (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Security Forces] an officer your contact trusts said his unit would 'wait for written orders' before acting — the trend settling and stabilizing
  - [Money And Logistics] This removes any serious doubt that approaching a breaking point — banks are imposing new withdrawal limits, citing 'temporary liquidity management'
  - [Street Mood] even the usual troublemakers seem subdued — the energy for protest feels depleted (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Information Control] a pro-regime commentator went off-script on live television and wasn't cut off — the control room is distracted
  - [Personal Observations] a well-connected friend said the situation is 'messy but controlled' and seemed unbothered — the trend settling and stabilizing
  - [Diplomatic Signals] foreign airlines have quietly added extra flights out of the capital — route changes driven by demand, not schedule (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Institutional Functioning] civil servants are reporting contradictory instructions from different parts of the bureaucracy — the trend settling and stabilizing

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - Whether the military's silence means they're loyal, undecided, or waiting for the right moment.
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: "I think we're seeing the regime's grip start to slip - the cabinet reshuffle debacle and the banks' new withdrawal limits are just a couple of signs that things are unraveling quickly. It's unclear what will happen next, but with foreign airlines adding flights out of the capital and people on the streets starting to talk openly, it feels like we're approaching a tipping point."
